classification.difficultyReason: Relate two journey times with a delayed start, generalise the separation and determine the catch-up distance.

content.prompt: Two cars leave Roma on the Warrego Highway travelling in the same direction. One car leaves the town 30 minutes before the other. The first car averages 80 km/h while the second car averages 96 km/h.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How far apart are the cars when the first car is:

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{First car's travel time} &= \frac{50}{80}=\frac58\text{ h}\\\text{Second car's travel time} &= \frac58-\frac12=\frac18\text{ h}\\\text{Second car's distance} &= 96\times\frac18=12\text{ km}\\\text{Separation} &= 50-12=38\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: $x$ km from Roma, assuming that the first car is still in front of the second car, and that the second car has left Roma?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{First car's travel time} &= \frac{x}{80}\text{ h}\\\text{Second car's travel time} &= \left(\frac{x}{80}-\frac12\right)\text{ h}\\\text{Second car's distance} &= 96\left(\frac{x}{80}-\frac12\right)\\\text{Second car's distance} &= \frac65x-48\text{ km}\\\text{Separation} &= x-\left(\frac65x-48\right)\\\text{Separation} &= \left(48-\frac{x}{5}\right)\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far from Roma does the second car catch up to the first?

answer.worked:
At the catch-up point, the separation in part a ii is zero.
$$\begin{align*}48-\frac{x}{5} &= 0\\48 &= \frac{x}{5}\\x &= 240\end{align*}$$
The second car catches the first $240\text{ km}$ from Roma.
